note: Third state off the federal gap list. 23 likely_rv rows: 3 were already in the database under the same recreation.gov id (the coordinate-only gap match missed them; the triage now checks ids), leaving 20. 16 campgrounds added from 14 rows plus the John Day basin bundle, which is four BLM campgrounds under one facility id. 7 excluded, each for a stated reason. Mostly Mt. Hood, Willamette, Siuslaw and Malheur Forest Service sites, plus BLM Coast Range and John Day sites and one USACE.

Yellowbottom is recorded as excluded, but if BLM ever reopens campsites there it becomes a normal add.

method_notes: recreation.gov's per-site 'Proximity to Water' attribute is the per-site flag the gate counts, and ten of these facilities carry it — but its VALUE is unreliable (Tollgate and Lazy Bend say 'Lakefront' beside rivers), and at Indian Henry it names a creek the imagery never shows. What made it usable was measuring each flagged pad against the OSM water line: Cape Perpetua 1-13 m (creekside), Tollgate 5-21 m (riverfront), Alsea Falls 27-45 m (riverfront), Still Creek 31-51 m (creekside), Indian Henry 20-41 m to Whale Creek rather than the Clackamas (creekside). Clear Lake's flags failed that test: 58-90 m behind a continuous pine band, so lakeview.

Two size-gate exclusions came from the AGENCY'S access notice, not the catalog: Eagle Creek's catalog lists pads to 120 ft behind a road with a 20-ft trailer limit, and House Rock's lists pads to 65 ft behind an entrance the FS says trailers over 20 ft struggle with. Read the rec.gov notices before trusting catalog lengths.

RIDB coordinates were wrong in three distinct ways this state: a facility pin 150 km off (South Twin Lake, already in the DB), per-site coordinates 4 km off at another park (Lazy Bend), and a bundle facility whose four campgrounds span 30 km (John Day). The bundle is handled by plotting it with sat_look --at <loop centre> and one entry per loop; recgov_hookups deliberately skips a facility shared by several entries, so those three take hookups from their notes.
